pyxsrt.py.summary: Extract the subtitle streams embedded in a video with ffmpeg/ffprobe.
details: Subcommands: ``extract`` writes every subtitle stream, ``first`` only the first one as ``<video>.srt`` and ``list`` prints the streams without extracting; the ``--naming`` scheme (indexed, rich or codec) controls the file names and ``--check-ffmpeg`` verifies the tools first.

The ``read`` subcommand decodes the codes of the given images or directories with pyzbar or OpenCV (``--qr-only``, ``--data-only``, ``--json``) and ``make`` renders a new code from the data with the ``qrcode`` package.

qv.py.summary: Page through the files of the current directory.
details: Reads every file (``-r`` includes the subdirectories), prints a header per file and shows the whole collection through ``pydoc.pager``.

rassingle.py.summary: Consolidate a multi-file package into one module.
details: Merges the modules of a package (or of a ``# File:``-sectioned dump), rewrites the relative imports, the ``six`` imports, the ``os.path`` calls and the logging setup to their current equivalents, strips the docstrings and injects the standard imports into the resulting single file.

re2regex.py.summary: Swap ``import re`` for ``import regex as re`` across a tree.
details: Walks the Python files and rewrites the import lines (``-r`` reverses it, dropping the ``regex`` alias back to ``re``), reporting each file it touched from a process pool.

reformat_txt.py.summary: Reflow ``.txt``/``.md`` files in place with sentence-aware wrapping.
details: Splits the text into sentences (the abbreviations and the inline code protected), rewraps them to ``-w`` columns (100 by default), keeps the headings and lists, converts the ``.txt`` files to Markdown with ``-m`` and offers ``--diff``, ``--backup``, ``--check`` and the ignore-file support.

remove_duplicate_functions.py.summary: Remove the functions of the targets that already exist in a reference file.
details: Hashes the normalized bodies of the reference functions, deletes the top-level definitions with the same hash from the target files (``-a`` applies, the default is a dry run) and processes the tree in a pool.

Subcommands: ``lowercase`` lowercases the names, the extensions or the content, ``images`` appends the ``WxH`` dimensions, ``clean-names`` strips the common prefixes and the junk patterns (release tags, quality markers) from the media files, ``jscss`` normalises the ``.js``/``.css`` names (and the HTML references), ``suggest-names`` proposes names for the ``.py`` files from their docstrings and ``pnr`` does the remove/replace/template renames.

repacktools.py.summary: Repack the installed packages into wheels, and the unpacked wheels back into ``.whl`` files.
details: The ``repack`` subcommand rebuilds the wheels from a site-packages directory (from ``RECORD`` or from the plain directories), computing the hash lines and the platform/ABI tags, and ``pack-dirs`` zips the pre-unpacked wheel folders back, with ``--packages``/``--all`` and ``--source``/``--site-packages`` selection.

repacopy.py.summary: Copy the installed packages into a wheel-like directory structure.
details: Finds the packages of the active environment (or of the local scan, ``--skip-scan``), copies their files plus the dist-info metadata into ``~/tmp/repack`` and reports the packages it could not find.

replacer.py.summary: Recursively replace or remove text in files.
details: Searches for the text below the current directory (or only in ``-f``), replaces it (or removes it with ``-r``), shows the surrounding context, skips the binary files and previews with ``--dry-run``.

report_git_files.py.summary: List the added and removed paths of every reachable commit.
details: Walks the history with ``git``, collects the added and removed files per commit (the modified ones are ignored) and prints the report or writes it as JSON with ``--json``.

reqmaker.py.summary: Write the missing pip dependencies to ``requirements.txt``.
details: Runs ``pip check``, parses the ``requires X, which is not installed`` lines, resolves the names against the installed package list (cached for the day, ``--no-cache``/``--refresh-cache``) and appends them to the requirements file, skipping the blacklisted packages.

reqmerger.py.summary: Merge the ``requirements.txt`` files of the top-level subdirectories.
details: Reads every ``<subdir>/requirements.txt``, merges the lines without duplicates into the root ``requirements.txt`` and with ``-r`` deletes the originals.
